html:
The hyperpyron was the gold coin of the Byzantine Empire from 1092 until the mid 14th century. Its name means "highly refined", for gold fired to purify it. Emperor Alexios I Komnenos brought it in to replace the old solidus, or nomisma.

The solidus, created under Constantine the Great, had kept its weight and purity for some 700 years and was trusted across the Mediterranean. But in the crises of the 11th century emperors mixed more and more silver and base metal into it, until by about 1080 it held little gold. Alexios scrapped the old system and issued a new set of coins in gold, electrum, billon and copper, with the hyperpyron at about 20.5 carats, a little less pure than the old coin.

It stayed a sound coin for a century and helped pay for the Komnenian restoration. Later emperors debased it too, and under the Palaiologos emperors it lost ground to the gold ducat of Venice. The last hyperpyra were struck in the 1350s.
